# Downtime: tier-aware offers — nominate one item per bucket so a budget-refused head cannot hide a root's backlog

## Problem statement

The coordination protocol carries **one offer per instance** (`coordination.ts`: `{instanceId, workItemId, worklogRoot, …}`, `COORDINATION_FILE_VERSION = 1`), computed as the single most important item in that root's Herdr head window (`computeMostImportantItem`). If that one offer is refused by a gate, the leader physically cannot see anything else in that root until the owner re-offers a different head.

The practical consequence is head-of-line blocking across **tiers**, not just across items. Observed on 2026-11-12: ContextHub offered an implement head (`WL-0MVMZLC410001BP9`, stage `plan_complete`); the machine-wide implement cap was full (2/2); every dispatch tick ended `host-budget-implement` while ContextHub held 5 `idea`, 4 `intake_complete` and 5 `plan_complete` candidates that no budget gate would have blocked. Those items were unreachable because they were never offered, and because ContextHub was not the leader (so its root was never swept) and was not registered in `downtimeWorklogRoots` (empty).

Per-tier nomination fixes this at the source: each instance advertises the head of each dispatch bucket, and the leader picks an **admissible** one, so a refused bucket cannot hide the others.

## Users

- **Implementation agents / the fleet leader** — need a candidate list that reflects budget reality. *As the dispatcher, I want at least one admissible candidate from every participating root so idle capacity is never wasted while a root's cheaper work waits behind a budget-refused head.*
- **Operators** — should not have to discover head-of-line blocking, and should not have to register every root in `downtimeWorklogRoots` just to make its non-implement work visible.

## Desired change

Tier-aware offers, version 2 of the coordination file, with **one entry per instance preserved**:

```json
{ "instanceId": "…", "worklogRoot": "/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub", "lastUpdated": "…",
  "offers": [
    { "kind": "implement", "workItemId": "WL-…" },
    { "kind": "audit",     "workItemId": "WL-…" },
    { "kind": "prep",      "workItemId": "WL-…" }
  ] }
```

- Buckets are the existing classifier outputs: `implement`, `audit`, and `prep` (the union of `plan`, `intake` and `risk-effort`). At most one nominee per bucket, so at most three per instance.
- The owner fills every bucket from **one** `getHerdrListHead(cwd, sprintWindow)` call (partition the window; no extra list fetch per bucket), applying the same per-bucket filters the single-offer path applies today.
- The leader iterates the offers inside an entry and applies the **existing, unmodified** sequential filter chain to each (classify → attempt budget → non-terminal cooldown → per-root code freeze → CPU gate → audit slot minimum/pin → review-queue hold → host-budget admission → CAS claim). No gate is duplicated, relaxed or reordered.
- On a successful dispatch the leader removes **only the dispatched offer** and leaves the rest of the entry in place, so a second tier can be dispatched on the next tick without waiting for the owner's 60 s check-in cadence. When an entry has no offers left it is removed exactly as today.

## Selection order — the decision this item must record

A fixed ladder of "implement > audit > plan/intake" is **rejected**. It is the same starvation pattern that `WL-0MW9X7EJ6009EL6E` ("Host-budget refusal early-returns from head scans, starving plan/intake behind an implement candidate") and the review-queue depth gate exist to prevent: implement-first inflates the review queue and starves the audits that drain it, and starves the prep items that feed future implement work.

The order must be admissibility-first (the continuable-hold machinery already does this: a refused tier is a neutral hold and the loop continues), with a **drain-aware tie-break** only when several tiers are simultaneously admissible:

1. `audit` while the root's review queue is at/over `browseItemCount` (drain the queue);
2. `prep` (plan/intake/risk-effort) when a prep offer is admissible (keep implement fed);
3. `implement` otherwise.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Schema v2, one entry per instance.** `CoordinationEntry` carries a bounded `offers` array (max one per bucket, max three; duplicate `(kind, workItemId)` pairs collapse). `COORDINATION_FILE_VERSION` becomes `2`. A v1 file (single `workItemId`, no `offers`) is read as a one-offer entry with its kind derived by the classifier, and is rewritten as v2 on the next check-in; no v1 file is ever dropped because of the upgrade.
- [ ] **AC2 — Buckets, not a second ranking.** Each nominee is the canonical first item of its bucket in the same window/order the single-offer path uses today. No new priority, age or scoring logic is introduced; `computeMostImportantItem`'s window, filters, stall-scan short-circuit and `{ok:false}` fail-open contract are preserved per bucket.
- [ ] **AC3 — One head read per check-in.** Computing all three nominees costs **one** `getHerdrListHead` call (a test asserts call count); no additional `wl` list spawn per bucket.
- [ ] **AC4 — No gate bypass, no reordering.** The leader applies the existing filter chain to each offer unchanged; a test enumerates the chain and fails if an offer path skips one. `classifyItemForDispatch` remains the single classifier (no bucket logic of its own).
- [ ] **AC5 — Drain-aware tie-break, as decided above.** When two or more offers in one entry are admissible, the selection follows audit-drain → prep → implement, and a test pins each arm. A fixed implement-first ladder is explicitly not implemented, with the rationale recorded in the item description.
- [ ] **AC6 — Remove only what dispatched.** After a successful dispatch the entry retains its remaining offers and `lastUpdated` is unchanged; with no offers left the entry is removed. Tests cover: dispatch-on-first-offer, dispatch-on-second-offer without a new check-in, and entry removal when emptied.
- [ ] **AC7 — Regression test for the motivating scenario.** With an implement cap of 2/2 and an offered implement head, a `prep` nominee from the same entry is dispatched; the terminal reason is never `no-candidate` for that tick.
- [ ] **AC8 — Fairness preserved.** Cross-root round-robin (`selectLeastRecentlyServed`) still governs root order; tier choice happens only **within** an entry, so no root gains an unfair share. A test asserts root ordering is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC9 — Legacy compatibility.** An old instance writing a v1 entry is still dispatched by a v2-aware leader (a v1 fixture is dispatched unchanged). `removeEntry(coordinationDir, instanceId)` semantics are preserved for stale/invalid offers.
- [ ] **AC10 — Cost measured and documented.** The added leader cost is documented (one `fetchItem` per offered item per tick: up to 3× today) with the measured tick duration at 7 instances recorded in the item as a comment; if the tick exceeds the poll interval, the number of buckets or the validation order must be revised before merge.
- [ ] **AC11 — Docs.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (offer contract, composition summary, the `COORDINATION_TIER_ORDER`-retirement note and this reversal) and `packages/herdr/README.md` are updated; the v2 schema is documented with a migration note.
- [ ] **AC12 — Gate.** Full project test suite passes via the dev-push gate.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — one entry per instance, `version: 1`, lock-file + atomic tmp+rename writes, `upsertEntry` / `removeEntry(instanceId)`, `pruneStaleEntries` (deliberate no-op).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts:153` — `computeMostImportantItem` returns exactly one item (or a stall-resume marker, or `{ok:false}`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — offer loop: file-order dispatch, `fetchItem` + `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` re-validation, continuable host-budget hold, per-entry `removeEntry` on dispatch, terminal-reason precedence chain.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.offer-attribution.ts` — rejection attribution (`withOfferRejections`) already exists and must keep working per offer, not per instance.
- Retired by `WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2`: cross-root tier priority and round-robin re-ranking (`COORDINATION_TIER_ORDER`, `coordinationTierRank`); helpers remain exported for tests only.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — v2 schema: add bounded `offers` array, bump `COORDINATION_FILE_VERSION` to `2`, migrate-read v1 entries, collapse duplicate `(kind, workItemId)` pairs.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts` — `computeMostImportantItem` output becomes per-bucket nominees drawn from the existing single head window.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-batch.ts` — the single `getHerdrListHead` read shared by all three buckets (AC3).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — iterates offers within an entry through the unchanged filter chain; drain-aware tie-break (AC4/AC5/AC6); removes only the dispatched offer.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.offer-attribution.ts` — rejection attribution stays per offer, not per instance.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` — `browseItemCount` review-queue threshold consulted by the audit-drain arm.
- Tests: `coordination.test.ts`, `coordination-leader.test.ts`, `coordination-cross-root.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.offer-attribution.test.ts`, plus new bucket/tie-break/legacy-v1 fixtures per AC1–AC9.

## Constraints

- One entry per instance, one lock, one file — do not split into `instanceId:kind` entries (it would disturb lease, liveness and `hasPeerOffer` logic).
- No new gate, no relaxed gate, no second ranking; the classifier stays the single source of bucket truth.
- Bounded work: at most three nominees per instance, one head read per check-in, no unbounded scans.
- Backward and forward compatible: v1 entries readable, and an old leader must not crash on a v2 entry (it reads the first offer and ignores the rest).
- All written output in UK English.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (medium): cost.** Up to 3× `fetchItem` spawns per leader tick. Mitigated by AC10's measurement and by the fact that refusals are cheap (classify only).
- **Risk (medium): protocol churn.** A version bump touches ~24 sibling modules and their tests. Mitigated by keeping the entry shape nested (no key changes) and by an explicit v1 fixture test (AC9).
- **Risk (low): starvation within an entry.** The drain-aware tie-break plus continuable holds make it impossible for a tier to be permanently refused while another tier succeeds (AC5/AC7).
- **Assumption:** an instance can compute all three buckets from its existing sprint-view window; if a bucket is empty in the window it simply nominates nothing for it (it does not widen the window).
- **Scope-creep guard:** the offer-only (passive instance) mode and the `downtimeWorklogRoots` registry both stay out of scope; each is its own item.

## Related work

- `WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y` — registered-root sweep introduced because a root with no instance cannot offer; this item removes most of that need for *participating* roots.
- `WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2` — dispatcher == Herdr list head (retired cross-tier ranking; this item is the deliberate, scoped reversal).
- `WL-0MW9X7EJ6009EL6E` — host-budget refusal starving plan/intake (the precedent that forbids a fixed implement-first ladder).
- `WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH` — dispatcher selection must consider every work item (whole-backlog window).
- `WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL` — single-leader election + coordination file.
- Discovered during: 2026-11-12 dispatch stall analysis.

Additional related work (automated find-related pass, `WL-0MWDDHVS4001J12W` is the notable new linkage):

- `WL-0MWDDHVS4001J12W` — docs item explaining which cross-root mechanism applies when (offers vs passive instances vs `downtimeWorklogRoots`); this item's per-bucket offers make that doc more necessary and it should cite this protocol (currently blocked).
- `WL-0MVP9UJ6S009LLK4` — peer-offer presence cancels no-candidate cooldown; the multi-offer entry keeps an entry alive across tiers, so the cooldown interplay should be re-checked after AC6.
- `WL-0MTII45EP002DWK6` — cross-directory tier dispatch; historical precedent for tiered dispatch across roots.

## Impact

Work no longer stalls on a single budget-refused head: every root keeps advertising its best implement, audit and prep item, so idle capacity goes to whatever is actually admissible.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "No interview rounds needed?" — Answer (operator, via seed context): the item description already contains the full design decision (per-bucket nomination, drain-aware tie-break, backwards compatibility), so the interview was skipped per intake step 4 ("skip the interview when the seed context suffices to draft a clear brief"). Source: pre-existing `## Desired change` / `## Selection order` / `## Acceptance criteria` sections of WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P.
- Q: "Duplicate check performed?" — Answer: yes — searched tier-aware/offer/coordination/bucket/dispatch terms; no item satisfies all twelve ACs (`WL-0MWDDHOK6009GJCC`, `WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS`, `WL-0MUJQFXYC009CFRJ` are related but distinct). Recorded as a comment on the item.
- Q: "Is the fixed implement-first ladder acceptable?" — Answer: no — explicitly rejected; the drain-aware tie-break (audit-drain → prep → implement) is the recorded decision, per the precedent `WL-0MW9X7EJ6009EL6E`. Source: `## Selection order` section.

# Docs: which cross-root mechanism applies when — offers, passive instances, or downtimeWorklogRoots

## Problem statement

The dispatcher now has three ways to make work in another worklog root reachable —
per-tier **offers** from participating instances, **passive/offer-only** instances, and the
operator-maintained `downtimeWorklogRoots` **registry** — but no single place explains
**which mechanism applies when**, what each one costs, and what each one cannot do. Today
`downtimeWorklogRoots` is the only cross-root mechanism, so it is documented purely as
"roots the leader may sweep"; once `WL-0MWDDHOK6009GJCC` (offer-only mode) and
`WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P` (tier-aware offers) are merged, that framing is actively misleading:
an operator registers roots that already offer work, and never learns that a
dispatch-disabled instance can be made to participate at all.

This item owns the **cross-mechanism operator story only** — the decision table, the
"choose this, not that" guidance, and the staleness/failure behaviour of the three paths.
Each feature item continues to own its own setting, schema and gates.

## Users

- **Operators** deciding how to make a root visible to the fleet leader.
  *As an operator, I want one table that tells me which mechanism fits my situation, so I
  neither register roots redundantly nor leave work unreachable.*
- **Agents and maintainers** reading the dispatcher docs to understand the candidate
  universe and the order it is walked in.
  *As a maintainer, I want the composition order and the per-mechanism limits stated once,
  in one place, so I can reason about a dispatch decision without re-deriving it from three
  sections.*

## Desired change

One operator-facing section in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (cross-referenced, not
duplicated, from `packages/herdr/README.md`) that:

1. states the canonical candidate universe and its order — scheduled prompts → offers
   (per-tier) → registered-root sweep → leader's own backlog — as the **single** canonical
   block, with the other mentions linking to it;
2. gives a three-situation decision table with an explicit recommendation per row:
   *root has an active dispatching instance* → offer (do nothing);
   *root has an instance with dispatch disabled* → enable `downtimeOfferOnly`
   (recommended) or register the root;
   *root has no herdr instance at all* → register it in `downtimeWorklogRoots` (the only
   option);
3. states what each mechanism **cannot** do — a passive instance still cannot dispatch,
   claim, reserve or lead; a registry entry does not make a root's instance participate or
   lead; neither can admit work past a host budget, code freeze or review-queue hold;
   and how each one fails (stale offer entry, undispatchable offer removal, per-entry
   registry drop);
4. documents registry operational behaviour: entries must be absolute paths that
   realpath-resolve to a directory containing `.worklog/worklog.db`, are capped at 32, are
   re-read every tick (no restart), and a bad entry is dropped on its own;
5. records the failure signature that motivated the work — "a refused offer head hides the
   rest of a root's backlog" — with the concrete 2026-11-12 observation, so a future reader
   recognises the regression if it returns.

**Placement (design decision).** The new section sits **after** the *Ranking contract*
subsections (*Whole-backlog dispatch window*, *Own-backlog fallback*, *Registered-root
discovery*) and before `## Architecture`, because it is the operator-level entry point to
those three subsections. It links out to `#### Offer-only mode` rather than moving it: that
heading is currently an `h4` nested under *Review-queue depth gate*, and relocating it would
collide with the composition/offer-contract rewrite already scheduled in
`WL-0MWDVN3N1004MBA9`. Re-nesting it is explicitly out of scope here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Decision table.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` carries the three-situation decision table with an explicit "recommended" per row, and the three "cannot do" limits.
- **AC2 — Composition order stated once.** The candidate-universe order (scheduled prompts → offers → registered-root sweep → own backlog) appears in exactly one canonical block; other mentions, including `packages/herdr/README.md`, link to it instead of restating it.
- **AC3 — Registry operations documented.** Absolute-path + `.worklog/worklog.db` validation, realpath normalisation, per-entry fail-open, `MAX_DOWNTIME_WORKLOG_ROOTS = 32` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.clamps.ts`), tick-level re-read (no restart), and that an empty registry is a byte-for-byte no-op.
- **AC4 — Passive-instance guidance.** The doc states that a dispatch-disabled instance offers nothing unless `downtimeOfferOnly` is on, points to `downtimeOfferOnly` as the recommended fix (registry as the fallback), and carries the security/safety statement that a passive instance can never dispatch, claim, reserve or lead.
- **AC5 — Offer-path failure and staleness behaviour.** The doc states how an offer path fails: an entry from an owner that stopped checking in is no longer treated as a live peer after 24 h (`hasPeerOffer`, `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS`), a non-dispatchable offer is removed eagerly at dispatch time without a pane or dispatched marker, and — under the v2 protocol — a refused per-tier nominee no longer hides the rest of that root's backlog.
- **AC6 — Failure signature recorded.** A short "why this exists" subsection describes head-of-line blocking with the concrete 2026-11-12 observation (implement cap 2/2, the offered implement head refused, 9 prep-tier `idea`/`intake_complete` and 5 `plan_complete` candidates unreachable), so a future reader recognises the regression if it returns.
- **AC7 — Cross-references and link integrity.** `packages/herdr/README.md` links to the section rather than duplicating the table or the composition order, every internal link and anchor added resolves in GitHub heading-slug form, no stale restatement of the retired composition order is left behind, and the downtime module-layout table gains no new rows (no code change).
- **AC8 — Accurate after merge.** Every claim is checked against the merged behaviour of `WL-0MWDDHOK6009GJCC` and `WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P` — command paths, setting names, constant values and limit numbers verified against `packages/herdr/src`, with no aspirational text.
- **AC9 — Gate.** Docs-only change: full project test suite still passes via the dev-push gate and the pre-push context budget is unaffected (this repo runs no markdown lint step, so none is claimed).

## Impact

Operators get one authoritative table for making a root's work reachable, so they stop registering roots that already offer work and stop leaving dispatch-disabled roots stranded.

## Constraints

- Documentation only — no code, settings or schema change in this item.
- British English, and the repo's existing deep-dive voice (headings, tables, work-item citations).
- Must not restate the feature items' acceptance criteria; it links to them.

## Existing state

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
  - *Registered-root discovery — sweeping roots with no running instance* states the
    registry's purpose and its validation, and carries the `candidates = offers ∪
    sweep(downtimeWorklogRoots) ∪ ownBacklog(opts.cwd)` snippet plus a four-row
    *Composition summary* table — the closest thing to a canonical order today, but scoped
    to the registry feature.
  - `#### Offer-only mode (downtimeOfferOnly)` is an `h4` nested under *Review-queue depth
    gate — producer review policy*, so the only guidance on passive instances is buried
    under an unrelated topic.
  - *Leader-only dispatch* step 3 restates the same order in prose a third time.
  - *Troubleshooting / operations* has the operator entry point ("A worklog root with
    dispatchable work is never served") but it only prescribes the registry.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — restates the order in the downtime worker bullet list
  (~"If no offer is dispatchable, the leader first **sweeps the registered worklog roots**")
  and documents `downtimeOfferOnly` / `downtimeWorklogRoots` separately in the settings
  list, with only a one-line hint that the two compose.
- `WL-0MW4ZOX45005N66T` — the registry docs child; its scope was the registry alone.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (low): doc drift.** The table restates behaviour that lives in code. Mitigate by citing the setting names and constants that AC3 pins, and by linking to the validator (`resolveDowntimeWorklogRoots`) and the sweep (`dispatchFromRegisteredRoots`).
- **Risk (medium): merge collision with `WL-0MWDVN3N1004MBA9`** (*document the v2 offer protocol*), which rewrites the offer contract, the composition summary and the README restatement. Mitigate by landing **after** it and re-reading the merged text before editing (AC8), and by keeping this item's edit to the decision table, the single canonical block and cross-references.
- **Assumption:** both predecessor items land as specified; if either changes scope, this item's table is revised before merge (deliberately blocked on both, transitively via `WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P`).
- **Assumption:** the `h4` nesting of *Offer-only mode* is left as-is (see Placement) — recorded so a later reader does not treat it as an oversight.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a "which mechanism should I use" table invites adding per-mechanism observability, decision-log tokens and troubleshooting for each path. That belongs to the feature items; anything genuinely new is filed as a linked work item, not absorbed here.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — new operator section after the *Ranking contract* subsections; condense the *Composition summary* table into the single canonical block; cross-link from *Leader-only dispatch* and the *Troubleshooting* "root never served" bullet.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — replace the prose restatement of the order with a link to the new section.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.clamps.ts` — read-only reference: `MAX_DOWNTIME_WORKLOG_ROOTS = 32`, `clampDowntimeWorklogRoots`.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — read-only reference: `resolveDowntimeWorklogRoots` (realpath validation), `downtimeOfferOnly` read.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.head-scan.ts` — read-only reference: `dispatchFromRegisteredRoots`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-tick.ts` — read-only reference: `runOfferOnlyCheckIn`.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — read-only reference: `hasPeerOffer` and the 24 h `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS` liveness window.

## Related work

- Blocked by `WL-0MWDDHOK6009GJCC` (offer-only mode, completed) and `WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P` (tier-aware offers, in progress) — this item documents their merged behaviour.
- `WL-0MWDVN3N1004MBA9` — child of `WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P`; owns the v2 offer-protocol documentation and the measured leader tick cost. **Boundary:** that item documents *the protocol*; this one documents *which mechanism an operator should choose*.
- `WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y` — registered-root sweep (`downtimeWorklogRoots`).
- `WL-0MW4ZOX45005N66T` — the registry-only docs child (predecessor of this item's cross-mechanism view).
- `WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL` — single-leader election and the coordination file.
- Discovered during: 2026-11-12 dispatch stall analysis.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQO9QK3N000V148** – Selection list does not update when item is closed in another instance (completed)
- **WL-0MWDVN3N1004MBA9** – Measure leader tick cost at 7 instances and document the v2 offer protocol (blocked)
- **WL-0MWDDHOK6009GJCC** – Downtime: check in and offer work when local dispatch is disabled (offer-only mode) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mst3oj8s0001rol, 0mvr8gdj3008wy3y, 0mwddhok6009gjcc, absolute, ac1 (+259 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mst3oj8s0001rol, 0mvr8gdj3008wy3y, 0mwddhok6009gjcc, absolute, ac1 (+248 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: absolute, ac2, active, actively, agents (+199 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed context (the item description drafted from the
2026-11-12 stall analysis) already fixed the scope, the three-situation framing and the
acceptance criteria, and every remaining question was answerable from the repository.

Decisions taken from repo/WI evidence rather than an interview, recorded for auditability:

- Q: "Is a separate decision table needed, or does *Registered-root discovery* already cover it?" — Answer (repo research): it does not. That section states the universe as `offers ∪ sweep(downtimeWorklogRoots) ∪ ownBacklog(opts.cwd)` but only from the registry's point of view, and never tells an operator when **not** to register a root. Source: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, *Registered-root discovery*.
- Q: "Where should the canonical composition order live?" — Answer (agent decision): in the new section, with *Registered-root discovery*, *Leader-only dispatch* and the README pointing at it. Rationale: those three currently restate the order and would otherwise disagree after the v2 offer change. Source: the three restatement sites listed under *Existing state*.
- Q: "Should `#### Offer-only mode` be promoted out of the *Review-queue depth gate* section?" — Answer (agent decision): no, not in this item — relocating it collides with `WL-0MWDVN3N1004MBA9`'s rewrite; this item links to it and records the `h4` nesting as known. Source: `WL-0MWDVN3N1004MBA9` description ("Rewrite the offer-contract and composition sections … of `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`").
- Q: "Is any of this already done elsewhere (duplicate check)?" — Answer: `wl search` over `downtimeWorklogRoots`, `offer-only docs`, `cross-root mechanism docs` and `dispatcher docs` surfaced only registry-scoped docs items (`WL-0MW4ZOX45005N66T`, completed) and general dispatcher docs items; no item owns the cross-mechanism decision table. No overlap requiring closure or rewrite.

# T1 — Generalised-budget test matrix (tests-first)

Testing slice for WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB: extend the host-dispatch-budget test suite
to pin the *target* generalised behaviour (all `DowntimeSkillKind` members capped;
absent kind = unlimited; audit-only over-hold) **before** any implementation
lands. Red tests define the contract F1–F5 must satisfy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit tests cover a capped `plan` / `intake` / `risk-effort` kind admitting below
  its cap and refusing at/over its cap with the unified `host-budget-<kind>` token
  (no `audit-host-saturated` anywhere).
- Unit tests cover an uncapped kind always admitting, never reserving, and never
  writing a ledger entry (no reserve/release bookkeeping).
- Unit tests cover the per-kind kill switch `0` refusing with `0/0` evidence.
- Integration tests cover admission on BOTH dispatcher paths (direct and
  coordination leader) for plan/intake/risk-effort.
- Tests pin the counting asymmetry: audit uses `freshCount` (no live-pane
  requirement, 2 h stale release); every other kind uses `liveCount` (live-pane
  release, pane-derived freshness).
- Legacy-marker tests are updated/removed to match AC5 (no references to
  `readActiveAuditMarker` / `isHostAuditActive` / `legacyActiveAuditCount` /
  synthetic marker counts remain).

- **Traceability (covers parent AC8 — tests):** unit + integration tests cover: capped plan/intake/risk-effort admit and refuse at their caps; an uncapped kind always admits and records nothing; per-kind kill switch `0`; audit over-hold vs live-pane release for all other kinds; refusal tokens unified (no `audit-host-saturated` anywhere); legacy-marker references gone; existing implement/audit behaviour with the default config unchanged. Full project suite passes.
## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.test.ts` — ledger/config/counting matrix
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.acceptance.test.ts` — behaviour acceptance
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.machine.test.ts` — ledger machine tests
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.test.ts` — hand-fired gate
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` / `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — both dispatcher paths
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.test.ts` / `host-budget-dialog*.test.ts` — observability/dialog

## Minimal Implementation

1. Parametrise the existing per-tier tests over all five `DowntimeSkillKind` members.
2. Add the uncapped-kind admission/ledger tests (expect no ledger writes).
3. Add kill-switch-`0` tests per kind.
4. Add counting-asymmetry tests (audit over-hold vs live-pane release for others).
5. Add unified-token and legacy-marker-removal assertions.
6. Run the slice's changed-scope test gate; document TDD outcomes.

## Dependencies

None (tests-first slice; runs red against current two-kind code).

## Deliverables

Extended green-after-F1..F5 test matrix; red-before implementation pins the contract.

# F3 — Legacy marker & token removal

Third implementation slice of WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB: delete the retired
`active-audit` marker readers and the synthetic legacy-marker entry count, and
remove the `audit-host-saturated` compat token and fixed two-key env overrides —

## Headline

A driven child's pre-push full-suite gate must judge only the mutation its own
run could have caused — currently a concurrent session's mid-run writes to the
shared main checkout are misattributed to the suite and block the push.

## Summary

A driven child's `implement.py finish` is refused when the pre-push full-suite
gate observes another live session's uncommitted edits in the **main checkout**.
The gate reports `live_repo_mutation` ("the test suite changed a guarded
checkout") and fails the run, so the push is refused — even though the child's
own worktree is clean and its commit is composed only of its own files.

Observed while finishing WL-0MWETWFSH007GRTR (tests-only, worktree clean,
changed-scope green): the full-suite gate failed with

```text
live-repo mutation detected: the test suite changed a guarded checkout for .../worktrees/wl-WL-0MWETWFSH...
  in main checkout /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub:
  added path [ M] docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md
  added path [ M] packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-storage.ts
  added path [??] packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.audit.test.ts
  added path [??] packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.audit.ts
  added path [ M] packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts
```

Evidence that the mutation is concurrent agent activity, not the suite:
`packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.audit.test.ts` has mtime 22:42:45,
four seconds *after* the suite started at 22:42:41, and the paths belong to the
host-dispatch-budget workstream (WL-0MWFJD1RV008FCCR, held by
`herdr-1794608223-1882173-11244`, driving children from ~22:17). No test in this
repo writes `.ts` sources.

## Users

- **Driven implementer agent (finishing a child in its worktree).** As an
  implementing agent I want my finish gate to judge only the mutation my own run
  could have caused, so I am not blocked by another session's unrelated work in
  the shared main checkout.
- **Operator / maintainer.** As an operator I want a gate failure to name the
  owning session or work item, so I know who is writing the checkout and do not
  hunt a phantom bug in a clean tree.
- **Downtime dispatcher.** As the dispatcher I do not want a false gate failure
  to burn a retry slot or re-dispatch work that is already correct.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The gate distinguishes changes that were pre-existing before the run, or made
  by another live session, from changes the suite made during this run, and
  fails the run only on the latter (the verdict is derived from a start-of-run
  snapshot of the guarded checkout, never from an unqualified `HEAD`/`git
  status` comparison).
- A driven child whose own worktree is clean and whose changed-scope gate
  passed is not blocked by unrelated dirty paths in the main checkout.
- When the gate does fail, the report names the owning session/work item where
  one is discoverable (e.g. via `.implement_state.json`, claimed items, or the
  main-checkout lock holder), instead of implying the running item corrupted the
  tree.
- A genuine suite-caused mutation of a guarded checkout — above all a
  tracked-file deletion/wipe in the main checkout (the 2026-10-26
  `packages/shared` incident class) — still fails the run: the fix narrows the
  false positive without weakening that protection.
- Regression tests cover both directions: (a) a dirty main checkout with a clean
  child worktree ⇒ the gate passes and reports the foreign paths as
  informational; (b) the suite mutating the guarded checkout during the run ⇒
  the gate fails and names the paths.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Agents stop chasing a phantom corruption bug when a concurrent session has the
main checkout dirty, and driven children are no longer blocked by work they
never touched.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: masking a real wipe.** Narrowing the main-checkout surface (option A)
  could let a suite-caused *addition* through. Mitigation: the deletion/wipe
  class (the actual incident) stays verdict-bearing, and the finish
  main-checkout guard (WL-0MVPE2CMY/CZ family) remains a second net.
- **Risk: actor attribution is unreliable.** Mid-run writes carry no ownership
  metadata git can read; probing `.implement_state.json`/claimed items is
  best-effort. Assumption: attribution is informational and always falls back to
  "unknown" rather than becoming a new failure mode.
- **Risk: pin/test churn.** Changing the clean→dirty direction moves a pinned
  characterisation test and a documented blind spot; the change must update
  rule, docs and pin together (see Constraints).
- **Risk: scope creep.** Options B/C expand into actor-attribution plumbing and
  isolated-worktree migration. Mitigation: keep this item to the false-positive
  verdict; record the isolated-worktree migration under WL-0MW4W15U500009D2 and
  any actor-attribution enhancement as separate linked work.
- **Assumption:** the guarded run's own worktree is the only checkout the suite
  can legitimately write; the main checkout is shared and may be written by
  other live sessions at any time.
- **Assumption:** "live session" is not directly observable; attribution uses
  whatever durable evidence exists (state files, claimed items, lock holder) and
  degrades to "unknown".

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken the wipe protection.** The main-checkout coverage exists
  because a worktree-scoped suite wiped every tracked file of `packages/shared`
  on 2026-10-26 (WL-0MVPE2BY9001CR9O, WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG). Tracked-file
  deletions in the main checkout must still fail the run.
- **Conflicting documented design decision.** The working-tree attribution rule
  (SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8.5) **deliberately
  retains** the clean→dirty direction as a mutation, pinned by
  `TestWorkingTreeAttributionBoundaries::test_clean_to_dirty_is_a_retained_move_direction`
  and documented as blind spot #2. Any change to that direction must update the
  rule, the doc section and the pin together in one change.
- **Plumbing-only derivations.** The guard's derivations must stay git-plumbing
  only (status codes + the start snapshot) — never a `wl-*` or path-name
  heuristic. If actor evidence is introduced, it must be an explicit, documented
  second signal, not a substitute for the plumbing rule.
- **Exactly one guard owner.** `guarded_run_all` is the single outer guard owner;
  the inner `live_repo_guard` plugin must apply the same rule and must not fork
  it.
- **Bounded cost.** The guard stays read-only git plumbing with no per-test work
  (the per-test fingerprint remains a trigger, never a verdict).
- **Fail closed.** `implement.py finish` must never push a checkout that a
  suite-caused mutation corrupted; narrowing the false positive must not turn a
  genuine mutation green.
- **CHANGELOG.md excluded** — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Existing state

- `guarded_run_all` (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) snapshots every guarded
  root before the run (`snapshot_guarded_roots`: the worktree plus, when it is a
  linked worktree, its main checkout) and diffs afterwards
  (`diff_guarded_roots` → `diff_snapshots`). `_detect_live_repo_mutation` renders
  the verdict; `implement.py`'s finish gate delegates to `guarded_run_all` and
  classifies `live_repo_mutation` as `GATE_FAILURE_INFRASTRUCTURE`.
- Attribution is **start-of-run provenance**: a path that was dirty at start and
  clean at end is excluded and reported under `live_repo_excluded`; a path that
  was **clean at start and dirty at end** (`status.added`) or is still dirty with
  a different code (`status.changed`) fails the run.
- The observed failure is the **clean→dirty direction**: the concurrent session
  wrote `.ts` sources into the main checkout *during* the run (mtime four
  seconds after the suite started), so the start-of-run snapshot was clean and
  the end snapshot showed them as `added path`.
- A single-owner lock exists for the main checkout during **finish**
  (WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84), but it does not stop a non-finish session (a driven
  child or the operator) writing the main checkout mid-run.
- A related alternative mitigation is already scoped: run the post-push/audit
  full suite in a pinned isolated worktree (WL-0MW4W15U500009D2, blocked; its
  tests in WL-0MW4W0WDF005Y0TQ, intake_complete).

## Desired change

**Outcome:** a driven child whose own worktree is clean is not blocked by another
live session's mid-run writes to the main checkout; a genuine suite-caused
mutation (especially a tracked-file deletion/wipe in the main checkout) still
fails the run; and a failure names the owning session/work item when
discoverable.

**Mechanism is an open design question (Appendix Q1).** Candidate approaches
(not prescriptive — the plan stage must confirm):

- **(A) Narrow the main checkout's verdict surface** to the damage class the
  suite can plausibly cause — tracked-file **deletions** and modifications of
  files that were clean at start — and report concurrent **additions/untracked
  creations** as informational, naming the owning session where discoverable.
  Keeps the wipe protection, removes the dominant false positive.
- **(B) Keep the full status surface, add actor attribution** (owning session /
  work item from `.implement_state.json`, claimed items, or the main-checkout
  lock holder) and fail only when a change cannot be attributed to a foreign
  live session.
- **(C) Run the pre-push full-suite gate in an isolated worktree** pinned to the
  would-be-commit (folds into WL-0MW4W15U500009D2), so main-checkout churn is
  out of scope entirely.
- **(D) Scope the verdict to the guarded root only** when the run started in a
  worktree, reporting main-checkout churn informationally — weakest option;
  regresses the 2026-10-26 protection, so not recommended.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `guarded_run_all`,
  `_detect_live_repo_mutation`, verdict → `live_repo_mutation` /
  `live_repo_excluded`.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `snapshot_guarded_roots`,
  `diff_guarded_roots`, `diff_snapshots` attribution rule,
  `describe_guarded_diff`, `excluded_churn_notes`.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — inner pytest plugin; applies the same rule
  and must not fork it.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — finish test gate,
  `_adapt_guarded_result`, `_gate_failure_reason`.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` — `TestWorkingTreeAttribution*`
  pins; the clean→dirty pin must move with the rule.
- `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` — outer-guard end-to-end tests
  (add the dirty-main/clean-worktree pass and the genuine-mutation fail).
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8.5 — attribution rule and blind spots.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — finish-gate and guard-ownership
  documentation.

## Related work

From `/skill:find-related` (automated report):

- **WL-0MVPE2BY9001CR9O** (completed) — added the main-checkout guard this
  item's false positive fires from.
- **WL-0MVPE2CMW006K25Q** (completed) — finish aborts loudly on foreign
  main-checkout deletions; already names the concurrent actor on the *finish*
  guard surface.
- **WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84** (completed) — single-owner lock for the main checkout
  during finish; does not cover non-finish writers.
- **WL-0MW4W15U500009D2** (blocked) — redirect post-push verification full-suite
  runs to a pinned isolated worktree; the architectural alternative to (C).
- **WL-0MW4W0WDF005Y0TQ** (intake_complete) — regression tests for the
  isolated-worktree verification run.
- **SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG** — the working-tree attribution rule (start-of-run
  provenance); the design decision this item asks to revisit for the
  clean→dirty direction.
- **WL-0MWFJD1RV008FCCR** — the concurrent host-dispatch-budget workstream whose
  writes triggered the observed failure.
- **WL-0MWETWFSH007GRTR** (completed) — the driven child whose finish was
  blocked by the false positive.
- **WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U**, **WL-0MV981ZGA007ARPG** (completed) — the concurrent
  `dev`/`origin/*` ref-exclusion regressions that must stay green.
- Docs: `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8.5, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`,
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (OPEN QUESTION) — which attribution mechanism?** AC1's suggested
  mechanism ("compare against a start-of-run snapshot of the guarded checkout, not
  against `HEAD`") is **already implemented** in `guarded_run_all` /
  `diff_snapshots`. The observed failure is the clean→dirty direction — a foreign
  session wrote files into the main checkout *during* the run — which the
  documented rule (SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG, `test-isolation.md` §8.5 blind spot #2)
  deliberately retains as a mutation and pins with a characterisation test. A pure
  start-of-run snapshot cannot tell a mid-run foreign write from a suite write.
  Which approach should the plan adopt?
  (A) Narrow the main checkout's verdict to tracked-file deletions/modifications
  and report concurrent additions informationally;
  (B) keep the full surface and add actor attribution;
  (C) move the gate to an isolated worktree pinned to the would-be-commit
  (folds into WL-0MW4W15U500009D2);
  (D) guard only the worktree root (not recommended).
  **Recommended: (A)** — it keeps the 2026-10-26 deletion/wipe protection while
  removing the dominant false positive (concurrent additions/untracked files) at
  low plumbing-only cost; (C) is the strongest long-term fix but is a separate,
  already-scoped item.
  Source: intake research 2026-11-15; no producer answer yet.
- **Q2 — how much actor detail is required on failure?** AC2 requires naming the
  owning session/work item "where discoverable". Which evidence sources are
  acceptable? (a) `.implement_state.json` / claimed work items only;
  (b) add the main-checkout lock holder metadata; (c) best-effort plus
  "unknown".
  **Recommended: (c)** — best-effort from (a) and (b), falling back to
  "unknown", so attribution never becomes a new failure mode.
  Source: intake research 2026-11-15; no producer answer yet.
- **Q3 — should this item fold into the isolated-worktree item?** Option (C)
  largely duplicates WL-0MW4W15U500009D2, which is blocked. Should this item
  stay narrow (false-positive attribution on the live guard) and leave the
  isolated-worktree migration to that item?
  **Recommended: keep this item narrow** — it fixes the gate's verdict on
  today's live-checkout path; the isolated-worktree migration is a separate
  architectural change with its own regression tests.
  Source: intake research 2026-11-15; no producer answer yet.

# Worklog push-side identity guard (moved from SorraAgents store)

> **Provenance:** this item is the ContextHub-home of SA-0MVKMVIAK005981E (`wl sync: guard the push side against sentinel worklog identities (t@t.com)`), moved per producer decision (2026-11-14): the change lands in the ContextHub worklog CLI, so the requirement record lives here and the SorraAgents tracking item was deleted. Producer answers on the three intake questions: **Q1 confirmed** — the sentinel/empty push refusal is absolute (fires even if the sentinel email hypothetically equalled the configured identity or an allow-list entry; policy forbids that state, pinned by SorraAgents `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py`). **Q2 confirmed** — the guard covers both worklog-data push paths (`wl sync` push AND `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`, the `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push` force-rewrite). **Q3 resolved** — tracked here in the ContextHub worklog; plan children live under this item and implement directly in this repository.

Planning is complete (`plan_complete`): see the plan-completion comment and the children. Full original brief follows verbatim.

---

# Intake Brief — wl sync: guard the push side against sentinel worklog identities (SA-0MVKMVIAK005981E)

> Discovered-from: SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2 (during the SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS epic).

## Problem statement

`wl sync` quarantines *inbound* worklog commits authored by an incident-era sentinel identity (`t@t.com` et al.) — the author-identity gate — but nothing stops a checkout that still carries a sentinel `user.email` from *publishing* worklog commits under that identity in the first place. That is the 2026-10-22 incident (host `RossGameDev` pushed `T <t@t.com>`; every other clone refused to sync until the refs were re-authored by hand) and it recurred with two further inbound `t@t.com` commits on 2026-10-23 (`dec50d4d6`, `893203e8d`). `scripts/check_git_identity.py` detects the state but is advisory and fail-open (pre-push hook only) — a direct `wl sync` (as agent sessions run) has no guard, so the push side remains the durable gap.

## Users

- **Operators** syncing worklog data from any machine/checkout — a checkout with a stale sentinel identity (e.g. `RossGameDev`) must be stopped *before* it publishes.
  - *As an operator, I want `wl sync` to refuse to push when my checkout's identity is a sentinel, so I never strand worklog data for every other clone again.*
- **Agents** invoking `wl sync` directly in sessions — they skip the pre-push hook and currently have no protection.
  - *As an agent, I want the refusal to name the identity and the remedy, so I can fix `git config user.email` instead of shipping a poisoned ref.*
- **Every other clone/consumer** of `refs/worklog/data` — the pull-side gate keeps working, but prevention at the source means no more blocked syncs.
  - *As a syncing clone, I want sentinel-authored commits to never reach the remote ref, so my `wl sync` never refuses on inbound history again.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A `wl sync` that would push worklog data while the effective `user.email` is empty or an exact incident-era sentinel refuses *before* pushing, naming the identity and the remedy (`git config user.email …`); the refusal applies when push would run (not with `--no-push` and not on the zero-change fast path).
- AC2 — The refusal never applies to the project's configured identity or to `syncAllowedAuthors` entries; the sentinel comparison is exact-email only (lowercased/trimmed match against the `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` set: `t@t.com`, `t@t`, `test@test.com`, `test@test`, `cache test@test.com`), never a wildcard/substring match.
- AC3 — An explicit escape hatch (`--allow-sentinel-author`) permits a deliberate one-off push, mirroring `--allow-foreign-author`: it never bypasses the empty-email refusal and it is audit-logged in the sync output/log when used.
- AC4 — Regression tests cover the sentinel/empty/config-identity decision as a pure function (Cartesian over effective/configured email × allow-list) plus one CLI-level refusal test; no network.
- AC5 — Documentation: worklog sync docs describe the pull-side gate and the new push-side guard together (remedy, escape hatch, and why sentinels can never be allow-listed).
- AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (ContextHub CLI suite for the new guard; SorraAgents suite remains green).

## Impact

Operators can no longer accidentally publish worklog commits under an incident-era sentinel identity, so every clone's `wl sync` stays mergeable and the manual re-authoring drill (2026-09-26, 2026-10-22, 2026-10-23) becomes unnecessary.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo delivery:** the fix belongs in the **ContextHub worklog CLI** (TypeScript: `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/src/...`, released as the `worklog` npm package), while this item is tracked in the **SorraAgents** worklog because the incident surfaced here. The implement workflow's worktree isolation is repo-scoped — the delivery mechanism (linked ContextHub/WL child item vs. cross-repo delivery directly from this item, cf. SA-0MVZEO59E004BCI8) must be settled at plan time, *before* `implement.py start` (precedent: WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K kept this exact question open until planning).
- **Sentinel set parity:** reuse the `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` rule from `scripts/check_git_identity.py` verbatim (duplicated in TypeScript — no cross-language import); keep both sets in sync via cross-referencing comments.
- **Escape-hatch symmetry:** `--allow-sentinel-author` mirrors `--allow-foreign-author` — never bypasses the empty-email gate, overrides config for that run only, does not modify `syncAllowedAuthors`.
- **No new dependencies; bounded, non-interactive; no network in tests.**

## Existing state

- **Pull side (guarded):** `ContextHub/src/sync/author-identity.ts` — `checkAuthorIdentity`/`enforceAuthorIdentityGate` refuse inbound commits whose author email is empty or foreign (allow-list `syncAllowedAuthors`, exact-email). Wired into `performSync` (`src/commands/sync.ts`) after the fetch, before any merge.
- **Push side (unguarded):** `ContextHub/src/sync/push.ts` — `gitPushDataFileToBranch` commits the JSONL export with the ambient git identity and pushes to `refs/worklog/data`. `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (the `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push` force-rewrite path) commits and force-pushes the same way. Neither checks the authoring identity.
- **Advisory guard only:** SorraAgents `scripts/check_git_identity.py` (owner SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX) detects sentinel/empty/mismatched identities, fail-open in `.githooks/pre-push` — a direct `wl sync` (the agent-session path) bypasses it.
- **Policy:** incident sentinels may never enter `syncAllowedAuthors` — pinned by `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py` (`test_incident_sentinel_emails_are_absent_from_the_project_allowlist`). Project allow-list: `250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`, `pi@local`, `sorra@thewizardscode.com` (`.worklog/config.yaml`).

## Desired change

1. In the worklog CLI, before the push step of `wl sync`, read the effective `user.email` (same identity git will commit with in the temp worktree) and refuse — with the identity named and the `git config user.email …` remedy — when it is empty or an exact sentinel match. Applies only when a push would actually run.
2. Pure, deterministic decision function mirroring `checkAuthorIdentity` (same input → same result for dry-run and normal modes): inputs = effective email, configured/expected email, `syncAllowedAuthors`, sentinel set; outputs = allow / refuse + reason. Guard order: empty → refuse unconditionally; exact sentinel → refuse unless `--allow-sentinel-author`; otherwise pass (non-sentinel configured/allow-listed identities are never refused — exact-email rule, no wildcards).
3. New `--allow-sentinel-author` flag wired through `SyncOptions` → `performSync`; when used, the sync output and sync log record the bypass (audit trail).
4. Same guard applied to the shared commit path used by `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (force-rewrite path) so a sentinel identity can never author any worklog-data commit.
5. Regression tests: pure-function coverage of the sentinel/empty/config-identity matrix (unit, no network) plus one CLI-level refusal test (`wl sync` with a sentinel `user.email` refuses before pushing).
6. Documentation: `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` updated to describe pull gate + push guard together; code comments cross-reference `scripts/check_git_identity.py` as the sentinel-set source of truth.

## Key Files:

- `ContextHub/src/sync/push.ts` — add the pre-push identity guard to `gitPushDataFileToBranch` (and the shared commit path used by `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`).
- `ContextHub/src/sync/author-identity.ts` — add the sentinel set (`INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS`) + the pure push-side decision function next to the existing pull-side gate (or a new `src/sync/push-authority.ts`).
- `ContextHub/src/commands/sync.ts` — wire `--allow-sentinel-author` (option, `performSync` options, audit log output).
- `ContextHub/src/cli-types.ts` — `SyncOptions` typing for the new flag.
- `ContextHub/tests/sync-author-gate.test.ts` and `ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-author-gate.test.ts` — pure-function matrix + CLI-level refusal (no network).
- `SorraAgents/docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — document the push-side guard alongside the existing author-identity gate (AC5).
- `SorraAgents/scripts/check_git_identity.py` — canonical `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS`; cross-reference (source of truth for the TS set).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX** (completed, high) — *Restore wl sync: main-checkout git identity was left as incident-era 'T <t@t.com>'* — owns `scripts/check_git_identity.py`, the advisory guard this item makes redundant-at-source.
- **SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC** (completed, high) — *Repair wl sync: allow operator GitHub identity, purge incident-era t@t.com commits* — established the pull-side allow-list/exact-email semantics this push guard mirrors.
- **SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2** (completed, high) — *wl sync blocked again: inbound t@t.com-authored worklog commits on refs/worklog/data* — discovery parent; the 2026-10-23 recurrence.
- **SA-0MVLJDS04002KI1W** (completed, high) — *wl sync blocked again: inbound t@t.com-authored worklog commits fail the author-identity gate* — 2026-10-23 second recurrence.
- **SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS** (completed, high) — *wl sync blocked: pi@local* — the epic this item was discovered during; `pi@local` allow-listing context.
- **SA-0MVVX9PAT009Q45H** (open, high) — *wl sync blocked: sorra@thewizardscode.com* — pull-side allow-list edge (deliberately allow-listed real identity — the carve-out pattern AC2 protects).
- **WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K** (completed, ContextHub store) — *wl sync to be run before refactor and standup skills* — precedent for cross-repo items and for recording delivery-location as an explicit question before implement.
- **SA-0MVZEO59E004BCI8** (completed) — *implement.py drive: refusal-aware finish recovery (cross-repo delivery record)* — precedent for delivering cross-repo work from a tracking item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **AC2 interpretation (recommended, pending producer confirmation):** the sentinel/empty refusal is **absolute** — it fires even when the sentinel email also equals the configured identity or an allow-list entry. AC2's "never applies to the configured identity / allow-list" carve-out protects *non-sentinel* identities only (exact-match rule); project policy already forbids allowing sentinels (pinned by `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py`), so the two clauses do not overlap in any policy-compliant state. Guard order enforces this: empty → refuse; exact sentinel → refuse unless `--allow-sentinel-author`; else pass.
- **Cross-repo delivery risk:** `implement.py` refuse changes outside the item's worktree; the fix must be delivered to the ContextHub repo through a linked item or cross-repo delivery. **Mitigation:** flag at plan time before `start`; record delivery mechanism as a decision in the work item.
- **Sentinel-set drift risk:** the TS set must stay byte-identical to `check_git_identity.py::INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS`; no shared import exists across languages. **Mitigation:** cross-referencing comments + a unit test pinning the exact set (as `test_author_gate_allowlist.py` does on the SorraAgents side).
- **Escape-hatch abuse risk:** `--allow-sentinel-author` could be used routinely instead of fixing identity. **Mitigation:** audit-log the bypass in sync output/log (AC3) + docs frame it as incident-only, mirroring `--allow-foreign-author`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "guard every git write in wl" is a tempting generalisation. **Mitigation:** scope strictly to the two worklog-data push paths (`wl sync` push + doctor force-rewrite); track anything broader as a separate item.
- **Assumption:** the effective `user.email` read at guard time is the identity git commits with — the temp push worktree shares the repo's config (including local overrides), so reading `git config user.email` from the repo root is sufficient. If a future git version allows per-environment author identity (env vars/`-c` overrides), the guard may need to consider `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`/`GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL`; out of scope today.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (AC2 scope — **CONFIRMED by producer**, 2026-11-14): "AC2 says the refusal never applies to the project's configured identity or `syncAllowedAuthors` entries. If a checkout's effective `user.email` IS an incident sentinel (e.g. the 2026-09-26 leaked-config state), must `wl sync` refuse anyway?" — **Recommended:** yes, refuse — the sentinel/empty gate is absolute and the configured-identity/allow-list carve-out protects only non-sentinel identities (guard order: empty → sentinel → pass). Rationale: sentinels are policy-forbidden from the allow-list (`tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py`), so the clauses never overlap in a compliant project; a literal carve-out would re-create the incident. Source: AC1 text (`user.email` set to a sentinel → refuse), `.worklog/config.yaml` policy comments, `check_git_identity.py` remedy text ("incident sentinels such as t@t.com never"). Pending producer confirmation at review.
- Q2 (push-path scope — **CONFIRMED by producer**, 2026-11-14): "Should the guard also cover `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (the `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push` force-rewrite) or only the `wl sync` push step?" — **Recommended:** both — either path publishes worklog-data commits under the ambient identity and a sentinel-authored force-rewrite poisons the remote ref identically. Source: `src/sync/push.ts` structure (shared commit path). Pending producer confirmation at review.
- Q3 (cross-repo delivery — **RESOLVED by producer**, 2026-11-14: moved to ContextHub): "This SA item is the requirement/incident record, but the change lands in the ContextHub worklog CLI. Delivery mechanism?" — **Resolved:** this item IS the ContextHub WL record (moved from the SorraAgents store); plan children were recreated under this item and implement directly in this repository (worktree isolation now repo-aligned).
- Q4 (empty-email bypass — derived, no confirmation needed): "Does `--allow-sentinel-author` bypass the empty-email refusal?" — No: it mirrors `--allow-foreign-author`, which *never* bypasses the empty-email gate (documented in `src/commands/sync.ts` flag help and `src/sync/author-identity.ts`). Source: existing code, `--allow-foreign-author` semantics.

# Tests: push-authority gate decision matrix (child of WL-0MWGO58KL00187CO)

## Goal

Test-first verification slice for the pure push-side identity decision function (parent AC4). Written before the implementation child so TDD RED → GREEN is observable: the tests target the decision function `checkPushAuthorIdentity` (contract below) that I1 implements.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A pure-function test suite covers the Cartesian decision matrix over effective user.email × configured email × syncAllowedAuthors × allowSentinelAuthor flag: empty email → refuse unconditionally; each exact INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS sentinel (`t@t.com`, `t@t`, `test@test.com`, `test@test`, `cache test@test.com`) → refuse by default, allowed only with the flag; non-sentinel configured/allow-listed/other emails → always pass (exact-email rule, no wildcard/substring matches).
- AC2 — A test pins the TypeScript INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS set byte-identical to SorraAgents `scripts/check_git_identity.py::INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS`, with a cross-referencing comment naming that file as the source of truth.
- AC3 — Deterministic: identical input yields an identical decision on every call (dry-run parity); the empty-email refusal is never bypassed by allowSentinelAuthor.
- AC4 — No network, no git mutation, no new dependencies; tests live in ContextHub/tests (new push-authority suite or new describe block in sync-author-gate.test.ts) and run in the ContextHub vitest suite.

## Key Files

- ContextHub/tests/sync-author-gate.test.ts (or ContextHub/tests/push-authority.test.ts) — pure-function matrix + sentinel-set parity pin
- ContextHub/src/sync/author-identity.ts or ContextHub/src/sync/push-authority.ts — contract under test (implemented by child I1)

# Implement: push-side identity guard (child of WL-0MWGO58KL00187CO)

## Goal

Implementation slice for parent AC1/AC2: refuse to publish worklog-data commits when the effective git `user.email` is empty or an exact incident-era sentinel, so a checkout with a stale sentinel identity can never poison `refs/worklog/data`. Covers the `wl sync` push path, the auto-sync/init callers of `gitPushDataFileToBranch`, and the doctor force-rewrite path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A TypeScript `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` set (exact: `t@t.com`, `t@t`, `test@test.com`, `test@test`, `cache test@test.com`; lowercased/trimmed comparison) plus a pure, deterministic decision function mirroring `checkAuthorIdentity` (inputs: effective email, configured/expected email, allowedAuthors, allowSentinelAuthor; outputs: allow / refuse + reason). Guard order: empty → refuse unconditionally; exact sentinel → refuse unless allowSentinelAuthor; otherwise pass — exact-email only, never a wildcard/substring match.
- AC2 — `gitPushDataFileToBranch` refuses BEFORE committing/pushing when the effective `user.email` (read via git config from the repo root, per the temp-worktree config-sharing assumption) is empty or an exact sentinel, naming the identity and the remedy (`git config user.email …`). The guard only fires when this function is invoked, i.e. when a push would actually run — `--no-push` and the zero-change fast path never call it.
- AC3 — `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` applies the same guard with no escape hatch, so a sentinel identity can never author a force-rewritten worklog-data ref.
- AC4 — Non-sentinel configured/allow-listed identities are never refused (exact-email rule); sentinel refusal is absolute — it fires even if the sentinel email somehow equalled the configured identity or an allow-list entry (a state project policy forbids; pinned by SorraAgents `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py`).
- AC5 — Code comments cross-reference SorraAgents `scripts/check_git_identity.py::INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` as the sentinel-set source of truth (no cross-language import; keep both sets in sync).
- AC6 — ContextHub CLI unit suite green with the change (parent AC6); the T1/T2 test children are green with this implementation.

## Key Files

- ContextHub/src/sync/author-identity.ts (add sentinel set + pure decision function next to the pull gate) or new ContextHub/src/sync/push-authority.ts
- ContextHub/src/sync/push.ts — guard wired into `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`
- ContextHub/src/sync.ts — barrel re-export if a new module is added

## Constraints

- Scope strictly to the two worklog-data push paths + their callers (`src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/index.ts` auto-sync, `src/commands/init.sync.ts`) — no broader "guard every git write" generalisation.
- No new dependencies; bounded and non-interactive.
- Parent: WL-0MWGO58KL00187CO (delivery resolved — this item lives in the ContextHub repo whose CLI it changes).

# Implement: --allow-sentinel-author escape hatch (child of WL-0MWGO58KL00187CO)

## Goal

Implementation slice for parent AC3: wire an explicit `--allow-sentinel-author` flag through the sync CLI so a deliberate one-off push under an incident sentinel identity is possible (incident remediation only), mirroring `--allow-foreign-author`, with the bypass audit-logged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — New `--allow-sentinel-author` option on `wl sync`, typed on `SyncOptions`, threaded command action → `performSync` options → the push-side guard decision (overrides the guard for that run only; never modifies `syncAllowedAuthors`).
- AC2 — When used, the bypass is audit-logged: the sync output and the sync log record that the sentinel-author guard was bypassed (identity + flag), matching the `--allow-foreign-author` audit-trail convention.
- AC3 — It never bypasses the empty-email refusal — an empty `user.email` is refused unconditionally even with the flag; it also does not bypass the pull-side author-identity gate.
- AC4 — ContextHub CLI suite green with the change (parent AC6); the T2 escape-hatch CLI test children are green with this wiring.

## Key Files

- ContextHub/src/cli-types.ts — `SyncOptions.allowSentinelAuthor`
- ContextHub/src/commands/sync.ts — `.option('--allow-sentinel-author', …)`, action wiring, `performSync` options, audit-log output + log line
- ContextHub/src/sync/push.ts / push-authority.ts — pass-through into the decision function

## Constraints

- Symmetry with `--allow-foreign-author` (overrides config for that run only; does not modify `syncAllowedAuthors`; never bypasses empty-email).
- No new dependencies.
- Parent: WL-0MWGO58KL00187CO (delivery resolved — this item lives in the ContextHub repo whose CLI it changes).

docs child of WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ (blocked-by the impl children).

## Goal

As a future maintainer, I want the two pane questions and the grace window
documented where the hydrator and dispatcher are described, so the
workspace-agnostic/workspace-scoped split is not undone by a well-meaning
"simplification".

## Scope (parent AC9)

- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` (hydrator section) and/or
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`: state that **demotion evidence is
  cross-workspace** (machine-wide `herdr pane list`, why fallback placement puts
  ContextHub panes in the Dispatcher workspace), that **display markers stay
  workspace-scoped**, and that the **claim grace window** exists with its default
  and its settings key.
- Record the prep-tier contract: intake/plan/audit spawns hold no per-child
  claim lock, so pane evidence is the only busy signal for those tiers.
- Add the new settings key to the settings table/section in
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (where `downtimeMarkerStaleWindowMs` is

## Goal

Make a genuine `anchor-unavailable` refusal **diagnosable from the log alone**:
carry a machine-readable detail naming the failing boundary (persisted workspace
missing vs unreadable herdr vs item-tab unavailable …) from the placement
resolver through to the `no-dispatch` decision entry.

Parent: WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH (parent AC6; parent "Proposed fix B").

## Context

`resolveDispatchPlacement` collapses every failure into `{ ok: false }`, and
`abortForAnchorUnavailable` records the flat reason `anchor-unavailable`. In the
reported incident the log showed 124 identical `anchor-unavailable` entries with
no way to tell a vanished workspace from a broken CLI — which is a large part of
why the wedge went undiagnosed for hours.

The decision-log entry schema (`CoordinationLogEntry` in
`packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts`) is additive/optional by
convention, so a new optional `detail` field is compatible with every existing
entry shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `DispatchPlacementResult`'s failure variant carries
   `detail: PlacementFailureDetail` — a string union of at least
   `persisted-workspace-missing`, `herdr-unreadable`,
   `dispatcher-workspace-unprovisionable`, `prefix-empty`, `item-tab-unavailable`
   (extended by the sibling mismatch item with `project-workspace-mismatch`).
2. The detail is collected from the anchor resolvers without changing their
   existing signatures for current callers — an **optional trailing report
   callback** on `getDispatcherTabAnchor` / `getDispatcherAnchor`
   (additive; callers that pass no callback behave exactly as today), collected
   inside `resolveDispatchPlacement` so no cross-dispatch state is introduced.
3. The recovery outcome from the sibling fix item maps to the detail correctly: a
   workspace observed **missing** that recovers successfully yields `{ok:true}`
   (no detail recorded); a probe that is **unreadable** yields
   `detail: herdr-unreadable`; a persisted workspace positively missing whose
   replacement cannot be provisioned yields
   `dispatcher-workspace-unprovisionable`.
4. `DowntimeDispatchOutcome` for a placement abort carries the detail, and the
   `no-dispatch` decision entry records it (additive `detail?: string` field);
   `reason` stays `anchor-unavailable` so every existing consumer, budget and
   starvation heuristic is unchanged.
5. **Diagnosable refusal (parent AC6).** When placement genuinely fails closed,
   the `anchor-unavailable` decision entry includes a machine-readable detail
   naming the failing boundary (`persisted-workspace-missing` vs
   `herdr-unreadable`), and a test asserts the field is present. The stale-anchor
   state with an unreadable probe records `detail: 'herdr-unreadable'`; the
   prefix-empty and item-tab-unavailable paths each record their own detail.
6. Tests assert `reason` is still `anchor-unavailable` and the claim rollback /
   host-budget release behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged.
7. No new barrel export, no changed export kind (split guard green), no `wl`
   spawn added.

## Minimal Implementation

- **Barrel-surface constraint (must not be missed).** The split guard asserts
  exactly 38 barrel exports (`expect(exported.size).toBe(38)` in
  `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.split-guard.test.ts`) and the baseline is
  frozen, so `PlacementFailureDetail` must **not** become a new barrel export.
  Declare the string-literal union locally on each side that needs it — a
  family-local alias in `dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts` (not re-exported) and the
  union in `downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` — cross-referenced by comment;
  TypeScript's structural typing makes them assignable where they meet, so no
  consumer imports a non-barrelled symbol (which would also fail the
  "exports every symbol a live consumer imports" gate).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts`: declare the family-local
  detail alias and add the optional report callback parameter to the two resolver
  functions (type-level only; runtime behaviour is unchanged when no callback is
  passed).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts`: report the boundary at
  each `return null` in `getDispatcherTabAnchor` / `getDispatcherAnchor`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts`: create the local
  collector, pass it to the anchor resolvers, return `{ ok: false, detail }`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`: forward the detail
  through `abortForAnchorUnavailable` into the outcome and the decision entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts`: add the optional `detail`
  field.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` — collect + return.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — forward to outcome/log.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts` — report boundaries.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts` — additive log field.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — detail assertions.

## Dependencies

- `Validate persisted workspace on read and re-provision` (the classification the
  detail names).

## Out of scope

- The project-workspace mismatch diagnostic (sibling item).
- Changing the `reason` vocabulary or any budget/starvation heuristic.

## Impact

An operator can now tell from the `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` alone why placement refused with `anchor-unavailable` — a persisted Dispatcher workspace gone, an unreadable herdr CLI, an empty prefix or an unprovisionable tab — instead of hours of identical undiagnosable entries.

data.description:
## Goal

Make the **primary-path near-miss visible**: when `resolveProjectWorkspace`
cannot match a worklog root but a herdr plugin pane reports a *different*
`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, record a diagnostic naming expected vs actual — and
document the operator remedy — while **leaving the matching rule unchanged**.

Parent: WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH (parent AC7 and AC8; parent "Proposed fix C").

## Context

`resolveProjectWorkspace` matches on the plugin pane's `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`
only. The ContextHub "Work Items" pane reports
`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD=/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr` (the
plugin directory), not the worklog root `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`, so:

```
resolveProjectWorkspace('/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub', deps, <same>) -> null
```

Other roots match (AH, RISE, TCE, SA), which is why only ContextHub fell through
to the wedged fallback. Fixing the stale-workspace bug restores dispatch, but
ContextHub panes then land in the `Dispatcher` workspace's `WL` tab rather than
in the ContextHub workspace — an invisible misplacement until it is logged.

### Plan-time decision (recorded)

The parent defers the question "broaden the matching rule?": **the rule stays
unchanged in this item.** Rationale: (a) parent AC8 explicitly makes broadening
conditional on an unambiguous ambiguity resolution, and two panes can legitimately
claim roots related by ancestry (this very project reports
`…/ContextHub/packages/herdr`, whose ancestor is the worklog root), so
ancestor/descendant matching would make ContextHub's own panes ambiguous;
(b) the item's user-visible unblock does not require it; (c) the operator remedy
is cheap and now documented. Broadening, if ever wanted, deserves its own item
with the AC8 ambiguity test.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Primary-path mismatch is visible.** A diagnostic is recorded when
   `resolveProjectWorkspace` fails to match a root whose plugin pane reports a
   different `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` (naming expected vs actual), and the failure is
   documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` with the operator remedy.
2. `resolveProjectWorkspace` reports the near-miss **only** when it returns
   `null` and at least one plugin pane reported a non-empty `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`
   that differs from the wanted root: the record names the expected root, the
   actual `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, and the pane/workspace ids. Reporting is additive
   (an optional report callback or equivalent), so every existing caller and test
   is untouched.
3. No diagnostic is emitted when a match **is** found, or when the panes carry no
   `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` at all (an absent env is not a mismatch).
4. `resolveDispatchPlacement` records the mismatch as a `project-workspace-mismatch`
   diagnostic detail on the decision entry (expected vs actual), visible even when
   the fallback subsequently succeeds — i.e. a successful fallback placement still
   logs the mismatch.
5. **Matching rule unchanged unless unambiguous (parent AC8).**
   `resolveProjectWorkspace`'s match semantics are unchanged in this item: no
   ancestor/descendant or prefix matching is added, the existing ambiguity rules
   (two panes claiming the same root resolve deterministically — focused first,
   then lowest pane id) still hold, and every existing
   `resolveProjectWorkspace` test stays green with no behavioural change.
6. `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts`'s doc comment states the
   rule is exact-root only, and that the reporting is diagnostic-only.
7. No new barrel export, no export-kind change (split guard green).

## Minimal Implementation

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts`: collect per-pane
  `{ expectedRoot, actualRoot, paneId, workspaceId }` near-misses while scanning
  candidates; report them when returning `null` (via the optional callback added
  to the resolver signature); keep the match logic byte-for-byte identical.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts`: forward the
  mismatch record into the decision detail (`project-workspace-mismatch`),
  including when the Dispatcher fallback then succeeds.
- Tests: near-miss produces the record; a matched root produces none;
  missing-env produces none; existing ambiguity tests unchanged.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` — near-miss reporting.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` — record forwarding.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` — resolver diagnostics tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — decision-entry test.

## Dependencies

- `Diagnosable anchor-unavailable refusal` (shares the placement-detail plumbing).

## Out of scope

- Any change to the matching rule, including ancestor/descendant matching
  (recorded plan-time decision above).
- Changing `send-to-pi.sh` or the project-workspace tab placement policy.
