Parent: WL-0MW8G1X3V007CGAE (Full-suite runs in an existing checkout silently use a stale @worklog/shared build).

## Goal

Encode, **before the guard exists**, the regression contracts for a shared-build freshness check that runs once per test invocation: stale build, fresh build, missing build, no discoverable repository root, and linked-worktree resolution. This is the test-first slice of the parent item (parent AC4).

## Scope

One unit suite, `tests/unit/shared-dist-freshness.test.ts`, driven entirely by temp-dir fixtures whose mtimes the test sets explicitly (mirroring `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts`). No test may read this checkout's real `packages/shared`.

The suite targets the guard API the next child introduces: an injectable function that returns `null` when the run may proceed, or the actionable diagnostic string otherwise. Red-first evidence is collected by running the suite before the guard module exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/unit/shared-dist-freshness.test.ts` exists and builds every fixture in a temp directory with explicit `fs.utimesSync` mtimes, so assertions never depend on the real checkout's build state.
- Regression coverage in unit tests with temporary fixtures whose mtimes the test controls covers stale, fresh (equal mtimes), missing-dist, no-repo-root and worktree-resolution cases; the stale fixture is asserted red-first so the guard cannot pass vacuously (parent AC4).
- The five cases are exercised explicitly: stale (newest shared source mtime newer than the resolved build artefact), fresh (equal mtimes), missing `dist/`, no discoverable repository root, and linked-worktree resolution (the resolved package is the main checkout's, not a worktree-local mirror).
- The stale case asserts the diagnostic names the resolved `packages/shared` directory, the stale artefact mtime versus the newest source mtime, and the exact `npm run build:shared` rebuild command from that repository root.
- The missing-build case asserts the same actionable failure shape and does not expect a raw `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.
- The no-repository-root case asserts the guard returns `null` (silent, fail-open) and never a false failure.
- The worktree case asserts the guard judges the resolved (main checkout) package rather than a worktree-local `packages/shared`, pinning the mirror-image false positive.
- Red-first evidence is recorded on this work item: the suite run against the absent guard fails, and the stale assertion is shown not to pass vacuously.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/unit/shared-dist-freshness.test.ts` — new suite with controlled-mtime fixtures.
- `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts` — fixture and mtime pattern to mirror.
- `./vitest.config.ts` — test discovery context (no change in this item).

## Test-first note

This item must merge before the guard implementation item; the guard item's acceptance requires this suite to turn green.

data.description:
Parent: WL-0MW8G1X3V007CGAE.

## Goal

Provide the pure, injectable guard that decides whether the `@worklog/shared` build a run actually loads is at least as new as the newest shared source file, returning either `null` (proceed) or one actionable diagnostic naming the resolved directory, the mtimes, and the rebuild command.

## Scope

Implements parent AC1–AC3 at the helper level and turns the red-first suite from the sibling test item green. Resolution must mirror runtime module resolution (`node_modules/@worklog/shared`), not assumptions about the checkout layout. The repository root named in the message is derived from the resolved shared package (its `packages/` parent), so a linked worktree names the main checkout that owns the build.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The guard resolves the `@worklog/shared` build through `node_modules/@worklog/shared` (following symlinks), so freshness is judged on the package the run actually loads and never on a worktree-local `packages/shared` mirror (parent AC2).
- The repository root used in the rebuild command is derived from the resolved shared package location, so a linked-worktree run names the owning checkout's `npm run build:shared`.
- Stale output returns one message naming the resolved `packages/shared` directory, the stale artefact's mtime versus the newest shared source mtime, and the exact rebuild command `npm run build:shared` from that repository root (parent AC1).
- Missing build output (`packages/shared/dist` absent) produces the same actionable failure instead of a raw `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` from the first `@worklog/shared` import; when no repository root can be discovered the guard stays silent (fail-open, never a false failure) (parent AC3).
- An unresolvable package or an unreadable directory also degrades to `null` — silent and fail-open, never a false failure.
- Equal mtimes count as fresh, and generated or declaration files are excluded consistently with `isDistFresh`'s documented exclusion rule, or their irrelevance is justified in a code comment.
- The sibling suite `tests/unit/shared-dist-freshness.test.ts` passes green, and `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts` plus `isDistFresh`'s contract remain unchanged.
- A code comment states the mtime heuristic's trade-off (a branch switch or restored file can produce a false positive that costs one `npm run build:shared`) and that content hashing is deliberately out of scope.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/shared-dist-guard.ts` — new guard helper module.
- `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts` — `newestMtimeMs()` / `isDistFresh()` precedent; do not change its contract.
- `src/cli.ts` — `sharedDistPreflight()` resolution-mirroring and diagnostic wording precedent.
- `tests/unit/shared-dist-freshness.test.ts` — the suite this item turns green.

## Depends on

The red-first unit-test sibling must land first.

Parent: WL-0MW8G1X3V007CGAE.

## Goal

Wire the shared-build freshness guard into every vitest invocation via `globalSetup`, so a run whose resolved `@worklog/shared` build is stale or missing aborts **before any test file executes**, with the actionable message and no side effects.

## Scope

This is the vertical slice that makes the guard observable end-to-end: configuration + runtime behaviour + verification evidence. It depends on the guard helper. The guard must run exactly once per invocation (`globalSetup`), never per test file (`setupFiles`), so it adds no filesystem walk to the 344 per-file setups.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `vitest.config.ts` gains a `globalSetup` entry alongside the existing `setupFiles`, pointing at the new setup module, and the guard executes exactly once per vitest invocation.
- Verified against a deliberately stale fixture checkout, the run aborts before any test file executes and prints the actionable diagnostic (resolved directory, mtimes, rebuild command) (parent AC1).
- All three `.pi/test-config.json` suite commands (`tests`, `packages/shared`, `packages/tui/extensions`) are shown to be covered by the guard, or a justified exception is documented.
- The guard performs no writes to the checkout: no implicit rebuild, and the working tree is unchanged after it fires.
- A fresh build proceeds silently, and an unresolvable package or undiscoverable repository root proceeds silently (no false positive) (parent AC3).
- The full project test suite passes with the guard wired in, after a legitimate `npm run build:shared` precondition; the verification run is recorded on this work item (parent AC7).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (parent AC7).

## Goal

# Unify dispatcher-anchor placement strategies and CLI helpers

## Headline

Extract the shared plumbing of the three placement strategies —
project-workspace + item-ID tab (`dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts`), per-prefix
Dispatcher tab and the machine-wide Dispatcher anchor
(`dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts`) — into a common find-or-provision-under-
coordination-lock helper, and unify the duplicated herdr CLI subprocess/parser
helpers, so naming/placement changes land in one module per concern.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the three placement strategies to share one
find-or-create-under-lock helper (and one herdr-CLI seam), so a naming/placement
change (e.g. the Dispatcher adopt-or-clean, WL-0MWHD0V41007ESWR, or the Ship
tab, WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU) is implemented once instead of three parallel
provisioning paths.

## Problem statement (drift catalogue, WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ)

- `dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts::getItemTabAnchor` and
  `dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts::getDispatcherTabAnchor` /
  `getDispatcherAnchor` each re-implement the same
  coordination-lock + double-check + create + persist-or-adopt sequence
  (`tryAcquireCoordLock`, `resolveItemTab`/`resolvePrefixTab`,
  stale-pane re-provision) with per-strategy persistence
  (`dispatcher-anchor.persistence.ts`); the find-anchor-in-tab probe
  (`resolveLivePaneInTab`) is shared but the create paths are not.
- Placement precedence lives in `downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts`
  (`resolveDispatchPlacement`) and reuses each strategy's result shape — the
  tie-in point for WL-0MWHW3PKX0048ZYL (deterministic placement).
- herdr CLI subprocess wrappers are split across
  `dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` and `pane-close-herdr.ts` (both run
  `herdr pane list`/`pane get` with overlapping parse helpers) and
  `downtime-worker.pane.ts::parseHerdrPaneListOutput` (already delegates to
  `pane-close-herdr.ts` — the exemplar pattern).
- Placement-mode post-processing (`applyPlacementMode`,
  `resolveExtensionsTab`) is a fourth drifted corner used by interactive
  dispatch only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — One shared find-or-provision-under-lock helper (e.g.
  `dispatcher-anchor.provision.ts`) implements the coordination-lock +
  double-check + create + persist sequence once; all three strategies
  (`getItemTabAnchor`, `getDispatcherTabAnchor`, `getDispatcherAnchor`) use it
  with strategy-specific resolvers/persistence — no parallel provisioning
  sequences left.
- AC2 — One shared `herdr pane list` parse/adapter (already the
  `parseHerdrPaneCloseList` contract) is the single pane-list entry point for
  anchor resolution, the reaper and the in-flight guard; `herdr` subprocess
  invocation is consolidated (one deps factory per concern) without a runtime
  import cycle between `dispatcher-anchor.*` and `pane-close-herdr.ts`.
- AC3 — Placement precedence and per-strategy outcomes are unchanged (pinned by
  `dispatcher-anchor.test.ts`, `dispatcher-anchor.probe.test.ts` and the
  split-guard baseline) — this child is structural reuse, not placement
  behaviour change (which is WL-0MWHW3PKX0048ZYL's scope).
- AC4 — Naming/placement needs of open items are accommodated at the shared
  layer: WL-0MWHD0V41007ESWR (Dispatcher workspace adopt-or-clean),
  WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU (Ship tab in invoking workspace),
  WL-0MVZ88G51004IYHW (tab placement left-of-extensions) — no per-strategy
  re-plumbing.
- AC5 — Full unit + integration suite green; split-guard baselines for
  `dispatcher-anchor.*` updated only where the extraction legitimately changes
  the public surface.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` — `getItemTabAnchor`,
  `applyPlacementMode`, `resolveExtensionsTab`
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts` — `getDispatcherAnchor`,
  `getDispatcherTabAnchor`, `resolveLivePaneInTab`
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` —
  `dispatcher-anchor.cli-parsers.ts` — `dispatcher-anchor.persistence.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` —
  `resolveDispatchPlacement`
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.provision.ts` (new canonical helper)

## Constraints & assumptions

- Structural refactor: no placement-behaviour change (deterministic placement is
  WL-0MWHW3PKX0048ZYL); coordination-lock semantics, ambiguity rules and
  fail-closed outcomes preserved exactly.
- Layering: sibling modules must not import the `dispatcher-anchor.js` barrel
  (existing split-guard constraint).

# Unify fetch/wl spawn management with pane-close herdr CLI seams

## Headline

Reconcile the fourth spawn/CLI seam — `fetcher.cli.ts` (`wl` CLI spawn with a
spawn cap, timeout, retry and in-flight memo) and the duplicated `herdr` binary
invocation helpers — with the canonical pane-discovery/herdr-CLI seams, so all
herdr/wl subprocess handling converges on shared deps factories and parse
helpers (or is documented as intentionally out of scope).

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want every herdr/wl subprocess boundary (pane discovery,
close, budget repair, fetch) to share one CLI-resolution + spawn + parse
convention, so a change to the `herdr`/`wl` binary probe order or output shape
touches one module instead of scattered execFile/execFileAsync call sites.

## Problem statement (drift catalogue, WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ)

- `fetcher.cli.ts` owns `runWl` (execFileAsync, binary probe `wl`→`worklog`,
  bounded timeout, spawn-cap slots, in-flight memo) while
  `dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` and `pane-close-herdr.ts` each own their own
  `herdr` exec helpers — three subprocess seams with duplicated binary-probe
  and error-normalisation logic.
- `host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts` re-implements label parsing locally and
  shells out to `herdr pane list` through yet another path.
- The pane-close CLI bridges to the Python `pane-triage` skill via its own
  executable — the CLI seam is the cross-language contract that must stay
  stable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A shared CLI-resolution + spawn helper (binary probe order, bounded
  timeout, exec seam, error normalisation) is used by `fetcher.cli.ts` and the
  herdr invoke sites; the `wl`/`worklog` probe and the `herdr` probe each have
  one canonical declaration (constants shared, not re-declared).
- AC2 — Every `herdr pane list` invocation across the codebase goes through the
  single parse contract (`parseHerdrPaneCloseList` family); the
  `host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts` local label parse is removed in favour of the
  canonical label module (see pane-label child).
- AC3 — The pane-close CLI output contract (pane-triage skill bridge) is
  unchanged and pinned by its fixture tests.
- AC4 — Where fetch/wl spawn management is deliberately different (execFile for
  data reads vs pane spawns via send-to-pi.sh), the difference is documented in
  the shared module header — no accidental convergence of unrelated seams.
- AC5 — Full unit + integration suite green; `fetcher.split-guard.test.ts` and
  the fetcher suites pin the refactor.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.cli.ts` — `runWl`, `CLI_BINARIES`, spawn-cap,
  memo
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.args.ts` — `buildWlArgs`, `getExecFileAsync`,
  `getWorklogDir`
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` — herdr subprocess seams
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-herdr.ts` — reaper deps factory,
  `createHerdrReaperDeps`
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts` — local herdr/label path

## Constraints & assumptions

- Behaviour-preserving; the `wl` CLI spawn-cap/timeout/memo semantics
  (F5/F8, WL-0MSGAEZRB0016GCX lineage) are load-bearing and unchanged.
- Pane spawns (send-to-pi.sh) and `wl` data reads (execFile) are different
  seams by design — this child unifies their *plumbing* (probe/exec/error
  convention), not their purpose.
